study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Brain Structural Phenotype of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using the Normative Model

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its aim to develop an individualized, low-dimensional metric by combining NMF with normative modeling to map deviations from typical development and to identify ASD subtypes, thereby addressing heterogeneity and clinical relevance. This satisfies both criteria: explicit objectives/hypotheses and the purpose of applying normative modeling (individualized deviation mapping and subtype discovery).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here, we combined NMF and normative modeling to individually parameterize neurobiological heterogeneity in participants with ASD. We hypothesized that individuals with ASD would exhibit highly heterogeneous deviation patterns... Finally, we applied clustering analysis to identify ASD subtypes."; "The normative model can map individualized variations relative to the normative range..."
cm1_research_objectives.location: Shan2022.pdf.md, Introduction and Methods; "Individual Deviations Estimated From the Normative Model" section

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and gender are explicitly modeled as covariates in the GPR when building the normative model. However, although the datasets are multi-site (ABIDE), site/harmonization is not incorporated into the GPR for the reference model; site is only regressed out later in GLM analyses of reconstructed weights/deviations. Thus, covariates are considered, but multi-site effects are not addressed within the model construction itself.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "...we developed a normative model by training a GPR on the ABIDE II TD cohort, using age and gender as covariates to predict weights."; "...the effects of covariates, such as age, gender, handedness, Full Scale IQ (FSIQ), and sites, were regressed out using a general linear model (GLM)."
